issues.description: _shutdown_telemetry removes all LoggingHandlers from root logger, mutating global state it didn't install.
issues.detail: The shutdown path strips every LoggingHandler instance from the root logger to avoid re-entrant flush deadlock. This silently removes handlers installed by other subsystems or embedding hosts. Scope removal to the handler this module created (hold the reference), document the deadlock path explicitly, and narrow the postcondition.

issues.description: _BufferingHandler has an unbounded in-memory buffer with no cap or eviction policy.
issues.detail: Records accumulate in a plain list until flush or stop. A slow hang or high-volume logging before session.start() grows memory without limit and can OOM the worker. Add an explicit invariant (ring buffer, max records, or max bytes) and drop-oldest with a warning. State the bound in the ADT contract.

issues.description: Replay path locates the OTLP LoggingHandler by isinstance walk over root handlers instead of holding the created reference.
issues.detail: _flush_early_log_buffer scans root.handlers and breaks on the first LoggingHandler match. If another subsystem installed one first, or ordering changes, the replay silently feeds the wrong handler or no-ops. Hold the handler reference created in _setup_cloud_tracer and replay into it directly; this also fixes the JobContext-to-telemetry boundary leak.

issues.description: Unrelated test/build changes (drop -n auto, exclude test_plugin_google_stt) bundled in a crash-log fix with no rationale.
issues.detail: The makefile change serializes CI and skips a plugin test with no commit-message justification. Bundling test-infra changes (and on Torvalds's read, a worker.py race fix) into a patch titled 'upload logs on session failure' breaks bisect/revert and obscures regression attribution. Split into separate commits and state why parallelism was removed.

issues.description: init_recording is overloaded as a cleanup-path flush hook, conflating setup and teardown responsibilities.
issues.detail: _on_cleanup calls init_recording with synthetic RecordingOptions (audio/traces/transcript False) to opportunistically flush crash logs, and init_recording silently branches into _stop_log_buffering on already-initialized or non-cloud paths. Split into a dedicated _ensure_crash_log_pipeline (or explicit teardown) so each function has one precondition and one postcondition.

issues.description: Bare except Exception around init_recording in _on_cleanup risks leaking half-initialized telemetry state.
issues.detail: The cleanup catches Exception broadly, logs, and only stops buffering on the failure branch. If init_recording raises mid-setup, OTLP pipeline state may be half-installed when shutdown proceeds. Narrow the catch, ensure _stop_log_buffering runs unconditionally before propagating unexpected exceptions, and log dropped record counts for audit.

synthesis.summary: The crash-log upload mechanism is the right shape — buffer early, replay through OTLP once recording initializes, force-resolve shutdown_fut on early crash — but execution leaks abstraction boundaries and lacks stated invariants. Three concerns reach consensus: _shutdown_telemetry globally mutates root logger handlers it didn't install; the buffer is unbounded; and the replay path locates the OTLP handler by isinstance walk rather than holding the reference it created. The patch also bundles unrelated test-infra and worker.py changes, hurting bisect and review. NEEDS-WORK: scope handler ownership, cap the buffer, hold the handler reference, and split the patch.
